R461.note: ECB replaced with AES-GCM correctly; hardcoded key explicitly left out of scope as a separate CWE-798 finding.

R462.note: Anchored allowlist regex rejects CRLF before the RETR command is built; closes the injection cleanly.

R463.note: ObjectInputFilter allowlist installed before readObject(); rejection path already covered by existing catch block.

R464.note: node-serialize swapped for JSON.parse; error/return contract preserved.

R465.note: CRLF/NUL check plus anchored address regex on both envelope fields before docmd(); correctly closes SMTP injection.

R466.note: Concatenated DELETE replaced with parameterized SqlCommand; return value and query semantics preserved.

R467.note: strnlen bounded to sizeof(name) correctly stops the overread; matches guidance pattern.

R468.note: Encode.forHtml() applied to the reflected Referer value in its HTML-body context; closes XSS without altering the surrounding format() call.

R469.note: json_encode with JSON_HEX_* flags is the correct primitive for the JS-string sink; closes both quote-breakout and </script> bypass.

R470.note: secrets.choice() replaces MT19937-backed random.choice(); ineffective reseed line correctly removed.

R471.note: Content-based detection (Tika) + re-encode + generated filename + storage outside webroot; scope assumption to PNG/JPEG is stated openly as the fix's own allowlist mechanism, not a silent restriction.

R472.note: crypto/rand.Int over a big.Int bound avoids modulo bias for the 37-symbol alphabet; correct CSPRNG substitution.

R473.note: Explanation explicitly claims the fix 'preserves current behavior for the literal foo call' but it does not: new URI("foo") is relative with no leading '/', so isAllowedRedirect's path.startsWith("/") check returns false and the only real caller (Case19A, which always passes "foo") now gets rejected with 'Invalid redirect URL' instead of the redirect it previously got. The write-up's own stated justification for why nothing breaks is factually wrong, which is worse than an undisclosed change since it invites a reviewer to skip checking it.

R474.note: AESGCM correctly replaces ECB. But the fix also changes ENCRYPTION_KEY from a hardcoded literal to `os.environ['ENCRYPTION_KEY_HEX']` read at import time with no default/fallback - if that env var isn't set the whole module now fails to import instead of the app running as before. That scope expansion (fixing CWE-798 key handling, not just CWE-326 mode) is mentioned only as a code comment, not flagged as a deployment-breaking change, unlike the sibling C# case (R461) which left the same hardcoded key untouched and out of scope.

R475.note: mysqli_query()/concatenation replaced with mysqli_stmt prepare/bind/execute; return/control-flow contract (null on no row, null on failed query) preserved.

R476.note: CallableStatement text fixed at compile time, header value bound via setString placeholder; closes structural injection.

R477.note: Captures the previously-discarded verify() boolean and short-circuits with 401 before claims are read; minimal, correct fix.

R478.note: length > frame.size() - offset check (post offset<size guard, so no underflow) correctly bounds the read before memcpy-equivalent indexing.

R479.note: Removes param from the format-string role entirely and HTML-encodes before println(); closes both the XSS and the latent Formatter-injection risk, and says so.

R480.note: Allowlist maps the raw header to a fixed, server-controlled procedure name before it reaches SQL text; placeholder mapping is explicitly flagged as such.

R481.note: Replaces hand-rolled SMTP dialogue with Jakarta Mail; strict InternetAddress parsing plus explicit CRLF-stripping on the subject closes both the MAIL FROM and DATA-section injection points identified.

R482.note: HTML::Entities::encode_entities() applied at the sink in the same rendering function; closes reflected XSS without touching the already-safe priority field.

R483.note: Removing the attacker-derived decoder.Entity map (rather than trying to sanitize it) is the guidance's prescribed fix; Strict mode still rejects any now-undefined entity reference through the existing error path.

R484.note: Control-character/backslash escaping applied at both logging call sites; SLF4J placeholder plus trailing Throwable preserves existing exception-logging behavior.

R485.note: Replaces both shell-invoking branches with java.nio.file.Files.list(Path); eliminates the sink entirely rather than trying to sanitize a shell string, and neither version wrote output to the response so behavior is unchanged for the caller.

R486.note: format_html() replaces .format()+mark_safe(), auto-escaping the interpolated value while the literal wrapper markup is untouched; correct Django-idiomatic fix.

R487.note: Statement/executeQuery(String) replaced with PreparedStatement + setString; finally-block close() and result handling unaffected.

R488.note: escape_filter_chars() applied at the point of interpolation per RFC 4515; closes both filter-logic injection and wildcard-based enumeration.

R489.note: text/template swapped for html/template with an identical API; contextual auto-escaping now applies to the reflected Subject field.

R490.note: html.escape() applied at each concatenation point in the manually-built HTML string; status field escaped too as disclosed defense-in-depth even though it's currently a constant.

R491.note: Same correct PreparedStatement substitution as the sibling Case01/Case03E chain; finally-block close() semantics preserved.

R492.note: Removes the billing-path CSRF exemption and supplies a CookieCsrfTokenRepository the API client can actually use; the now-required X-XSRF-TOKEN header is the correct, disclosed consequence of closing CSRF, not an incidental behavior change.

R493.note: Dropping the shell and using ArgumentList closes both metacharacter and (via the IP format) flag injection. But constraining `host` to a parseable IP address is a stricter requirement than CWE-78 itself demands (a hostname passed via ArgumentList with no shell would already be immune to metacharacter injection); this rejects any caller who previously pinged by hostname, which the write-up frames as an assumption about the endpoint's need rather than a required consequence of the fix.

R494.note: escapeHTML() applied to both reflected fields (note and the already-vulnerable ticket_id) at the point of output; correct for the plain HTML-body context.

R495.note: Allowlist restricts sendRedirect to http/https plus the exact fetch-source host (www.example.org/example.org), matching the case's own upstream URL; rejects relative/js/data schemes too.

R496.note: Removes the token-controlled jku-based IssuerSigningKeyResolver and replaces it with a fixed, out-of-band trusted key set; correctly stops the token from vouching for its own verification key.

R497.note: Rejects negative offset before the unsigned cast, then bounds length via subtraction instead of the overflow-prone addition; out_capacity check unchanged.

R498.note: Sort column resolved through a fixed, case-insensitive allowlist map before interpolation; already-correct @AccountId/@Query bindings untouched, and the map's case-insensitive keys still match the pre-existing legitimate values.

R499.note: DES/CBC/static-zero-IV replaced with AES-256-GCM; SHA-256 key-length normalization and random per-call nonce are disclosed, and the change also incidentally fixes a latent block-alignment panic in the original CryptBlocks call.

R500.note: calloc(count, sizeof(ProductRow)) replaces the unchecked count*sizeof multiplication, so an overflowing count now fails allocation instead of undersizing the buffer; existing NULL-check path handles it unchanged.
